Use Image 1 as the base image and change only the character’s facial expression to match the facial expression of the person in Image 2.

Strictly reference the expression, emotional state, mouth shape, eye expression, and eyebrow movement from Image 2, while keeping the identity and original facial features of the person in Image 1 completely unchanged.

Everything else in Image 1 must remain exactly the same, including the person’s identity, face shape, facial features and proportions, hairstyle, skin tone, body proportions, pose, hand position, clothing, accessories, background, composition, camera angle, shot scale, lighting, colors, and aspect ratio.

Do not change the person’s position, pose, viewpoint, or any area unrelated to the facial expression. The final result must look natural and realistic, with only the facial expression changed — do not replace or alter the person’s identity or facial structure.

Except for the subtle changes to the mouth, eye area, and eyebrows that are naturally required to reproduce the reference expression, no other facial features or areas should be modified.
